ref.quote: Bijdrage voor het binnenlands vervoer van reizigers met treinen van de gewone dienst ten gunste van de NMBS ... Deelname van de Staat in het kapitaal van de NMBS met oog op de financiering van de investeringen ... Deelname van de Staat in het kapitaal van Infrabel met het oog op de financiering van de investeringen ... Bijdrage voor maatregelen die strekken tot het kosteloos woon-werkverkeer per trein
ref.note: The rail amounts follow the public service contract between SNCB and the State and the performance contract between Infrabel and the State (pp. 140-142), so they are set for several years and indexed. 'Tracks and trains' simplifies the investment allocations (Infrabel: infrastructure; SNCB: its own investments, which also cover stations). Not phrased: bpost management contract payment (B.A. 33.41.52.312207), skeyes, Beliris/Metro Noord, PPP availability fees (Diabolo, Liefkenshoek), night-train subsidies, road safety and aviation administration. A 4th phrase was kept because free commuting is a separate, tangible allocation; drop it if 3 are preferred. Second check: 'tracks' replaced by 'rail network' because Infrabel's investment allocation covers the whole infrastructure, not only tracks; SNCB's investments also include stations (see B.A. 33 51 17 51.11.05 'Investeringen NMBS leefbare en veilige stations', p. 918), which the phrase does not list for brevity. The free-commuting allocation's French label says 'mesures permettant de tendre vers la gratuité' (measures towards free commuting), so it supports free commuting rather than making all commuting free; the phrase 'support for free home-to-work train travel' stays within that. corrected: investment phrase 'tracks and trains' changed to 'the rail network and trains' (Infrabel invests in the whole infrastructure, not just tracks) (flag 5). Free home-to-work phrase confirmed: grounded in B.A. 33 51 10 31.21.07 (p. 917, 'kosteloos woon-werkverkeer per trein'), neutral; kept as a 4th phrase. All five allocations confirmed on p. 917, contracts on pp. 140-142; phrases describe what the contracts pay for and do not suggest automatic changes (flag 3).
